# /crav1-update-kit

[All skills](../skills.md) · Walkthrough: [Update the installed kit](../../from-update-kit.md) · Playbook: [`SKILL.md`](../../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-update-kit/SKILL.md)

## Purpose

Update the installed kit on the current branch to a published release.

1.204.0: Codex is installed. `.crav1/kit.json` lists the vendors. A missing file is inferred from marker files and written in the same yes. `add codex` copies `vendors/codex/` into `.agents/skills/` and does not upgrade the other vendors. `remove codex` deletes kit-owned files that still match the release; a local edit is a clash (`keep` or `take`); other files stay. `detect` adds `vendors_from`. The project `AGENTS.md` is never written. Copilot is not installed by this release.

1.201.0: `vendors.json` lists each host: the folders the kit owns, the frontmatter a skill needs, the command prefix, and extra files. Cursor and Claude Code reproduce the 1.200 allow-list. Codex and Copilot are rows and are not installed. `detect` reports `vendors`. `vendors --root .` lists each folder and skill count and writes nothing. `--vendor codex` prints `$crav1-` on a Run next script; the default prefix stays `/`.

1.178.0: a stale commit-style rule is written, removed and committed by the kit itself instead of being refused as a project file; a stale rule whose asset is gone from the new release is listed under `delete`. The run ends `Run next: nothing needed now.`, never a `Next:` line.

1.176.0: a persisted commit-style rule that is the old release's copy, or names the missing `crav1-draft-commit-message/` skill, is rewritten from the current message-only asset in the same yes. A rule changed by hand is left and listed in `style_rules_left`.

**[`/crav1-update-kit`](crav1-update-kit.md)** takes an optional `to vX.Y.Z`. With no version, the target is the latest published release tag. `main`, a branch, a commit, and an open pull request are refused in one line. It detects the installed version from `plugin.json` or the `Kit version:` line in `crav1-docs/reference/workflow.md` (the changelog heading when that line is missing).

It commits on the current branch and does not switch. Before any write it shows which branch that is, that only this branch gets the new kit, and that other branches stay on the old kit until this branch is merged into them (merge develop into the branch; never rebase). It suggests merging first or switching branch when this branch should not move, and it warns about uncommitted changes. A yes from an agent or an earlier chat does not count.

Kit-owned files are three-way merged against the previous release. Non-overlapping edits combine. A clash shows both sides; the recommendation keeps the local side. A copied `docs/specs/_template/` or `docs/system/_template/` file is replaced only when it still matches the old release apart from line endings. Specs, walk-progress, build-progress, plans, tasks, notes, playbooks, and the build map are not part of the replace.

A plugin or user-scope install is not a commit. The command compares versions, says how to refresh or recopy, and still offers migration steps. After the replace, migration steps for the jump are dry-run, listed, and written only on yes. They are not staged into the kit commit.

The commit message is `Update CRAV1 kit vA to vB`. The script does not push. A push happens only when the user already asked for it in this run. The default ending is a local commit and stop. The heads-up card is not skipped by a word in the opening message. The yes is the user's answer after the branch is shown.

1.132.0: the first jump, before the command is installed, has a Windows PowerShell download next to the bash one. In Windows PowerShell 5.1, `curl` is an alias for `Invoke-WebRequest`. On Windows, use `python` or `py`. The three-way compare treats CRLF and LF as the same text. A line-ending-only difference is an update, not a clash. A real edit on the same lines still clashes. The written file keeps the local line endings. `fetch` clones with `core.autocrlf=false`.

1.190.0: `fetch` clones into a short temp folder by default with `core.longpaths=true` and `core.autocrlf=false`, and refuses an incomplete checkout (git status not clean) before any plan. The `ending` move tells the user to reload the window after an update and names [`/crav1-design-architecture`](crav1-design-architecture.md) resume <topic>` for open design topics.

## Runs when

The installed kit should move to a published release. Called by the user, or by a guild agent. The user's yes in this run is still required before a write, a commit, or a push.

## Prompts

Prompt budget: 2 (the most prompts in one run, the closing yes included). A prompt may hold several questions. See the asking rule in `crav1.mdc`.

## Reads

In short: The installed version, the published release tags, and the kit files on this branch.

Reads `plugin.json` or the `Kit version:` line, the published `vX.Y.Z` tags, the old release, the new release, `vendors.json`, `.crav1/kit.json` when it exists, and the working tree. It does not read a branch or an open pull request as a target.

## Writes

In short: Kit-owned files on this branch, `.crav1/kit.json`, the Codex tree when Codex is selected, a copied template that still matches the old release apart from line endings, an optional migration after a separate yes, and one local commit.

Writes kit-owned files on the current branch after a yes, including the Codex tree under `.agents/skills/` when Codex is selected, writes `.crav1/kit.json`, replaces a copied template that still matches the old release apart from line endings, and commits `Update CRAV1 kit vA to vB` when the user chose the commit. `add codex` commits `Add CRAV1 kit vendor codex vX.Y.Z`. `remove codex` commits `Remove CRAV1 kit vendor codex vX.Y.Z`. A migration listed for the jump is dry-run and written only on its own yes, and is left unstaged.

## Does not

Leaves specs, `walk-progress.md`, `build-progress/`, plans, tasks, notes, playbooks, the build map, persist rules (except a stale commit-style rule, 1.176.0), the transfer data policy, `kit-maintainer.mdc`, and the project's `AGENTS.md` alone. A skill folder that does not start with `crav1-` stays a project file. Copilot is not installed by this release. Does not switch branches, rebase, or push. A plugin install gets no kit commit.

Limits and exceptions: a target that is not a published release tag stops in one line. A clash is not overwritten. An edited template is listed and left. The kit source checkout is refused. An agent's yes does not write, commit, or push.
